title: Ajit Agarkar to Exit as India's Chief Selector After Defining Three Years
excerpt: The 48-year-old has told the BCCI he will not seek an extension when his contract ends on October 4, ending a tenure that delivered two T20 World Cups, the Champions Trophy and some of Indian cricket's boldest selection calls.
body:
• Ajit Agarkar has informed the BCCI he will not continue as chairman of the senior men's selection committee after his contract ends on October 4, closing a tenure that began in July 2023.
  • Under his panel, India won the T20 World Cups of 2024 and 2026, the 2025 Champions Trophy and Asia Cups in 2023 and 2025, while navigating the exits of Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Ravichandran Ashwin from key formats.
  • His defining calls included backing Suryakumar Yadav as T20I captain, elevating Shubman Gill to lead Tests and ODIs, making domestic cricket mandatory for stars, and deciding to look beyond Rohit Sharma for the 2027 ODI World Cup.
  • The BCCI's office-bearers are authorized to choose his successor, with Parthiv Patel and Pragyan Ojha emerging as leading contenders.

Ajit Agarkar has decided to walk away from one of the most scrutinized jobs in Indian cricket. The former India pacer, who has chaired the BCCI's senior men's selection committee since July 2023, has told the board he does not want to continue once his contract ends on October 4, according to The Hindu. The decision, first conveyed to officials in February and confirmed ahead of Friday's Annual General Meeting in Mumbai, closes a three-year stint defined by bold calls and major silverware.

The call to step aside

"Agarkar has informed the BCCI just before the Annual General Meeting that he is not willing to continue as a selector after the conclusion of his term on October 4," a BCCI office-bearer told The Hindu. In his communication, Agarkar cited discussions dating back to February, when he first asked the board to line up alternatives, according to the Hindustan Times.

The board's 95th AGM authorized its office-bearers to take the final call, but secretary Devajit Saikia offered no timeline: "We still have 15 days to go. Fifteen days is a long time in the world of cricket. We have time. We will make a decision and, at the appropriate time, we will let you know."

"Fifteen days is a long time in the world of cricket. We have time. We will make a decision and, at the appropriate time, we will let you know."

— Devajit Saikia, BCCI Secretary

Agarkar's last meeting as chairman may already be behind him — he picked India's squads this week for the West Indies white-ball series and the Irani Cup starting October 1. Former wicketkeeper-batter Parthiv Patel is reported as the front-runner to succeed him, with ex-spinner Pragyan Ojha, already on the panel, also in contention.

Silverware amid transition

By results, this was the most successful selection tenure in modern Indian cricket. India won the T20 World Cup in 2024, the Champions Trophy in 2025 and the T20 World Cup again in 2026 — beating New Zealand by 96 runs in the final — plus Asia Cups in 2023 and 2025, and finished runners-up at the 2023 ODI World Cup. The ledger's other side: home Test whitewashes against New Zealand (3-0) and South Africa (2-0), and a generational handover that saw Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli retire from Tests and T20Is and Ravichandran Ashwin call time on his India career.

The decisions that defined him

Agarkar will be remembered less for the trophies than for the conviction behind the calls. He backed Suryakumar Yadav as T20I captain over Hardik Pandya — criticized at the time, validated by two World Cup titles — then moved on to Shreyas Iyer when Surya's batting form faded. He elevated Shubman Gill to the Test and ODI captaincy; Gill answered with 700 runs in the England series. He backed Abhishek Sharma as T20I opener, gave Sanju Samson the long rope his talent deserved, and made domestic cricket non-negotiable — even for Kohli and Rishabh Pant, who turned out in the Ranji Trophy.

The most sensitive call concerned Rohit Sharma. After the England tour in July, the panel reportedly decided India should look beyond Rohit for the 2027 ODI World Cup in Africa, doubting he could sustain fitness and form through next October and November. The move backfired when Rohit's meeting with the BCCI leadership, followed by a century at Lord's, forced the selectors to retreat — a rare public reversal. Rohit remains in the squad for the home ODI series against the West Indies starting September 27.

"What underpinned Agarkar's time in the job was clarity in decision-making, adherence to processes, clear communication with players, and transparency with the public, while protecting the confidentiality of the ecosystem."

— The Economic Times

What comes next

The BCCI has about two weeks to decide, with a full tour of New Zealand — five T20Is, five ODIs, two Tests — beginning in mid-October and 2027 World Cup planning already underway. For diaspora fans who pack stadiums whenever India tours, the next chief selector will shape the team they watch for years. The office-bearers have their mandate; the decision, as Saikia put it, will come "at the appropriate time."
